answer: Whether agents trade water in an oasis or power on the tundra, the allocation kernel weights votes by escrowed stake, not account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 units of voting power. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens for the full voting period, tying up capital instead of minting free identities. Wealth can still buy control, but extra names alone cannot.
